title: Engineering a manganese superoxide dismutase with enhanced thermostability and activity via protein language Models: Toward antioxidant and anti-inflammatory applications in biomedicine and skincare.
authors: Zhang, Naying; Deng, Yuting; Li, Rui; Liu, Fan; Wei, Dongsheng; Ren, Zefeng; Jin, Xuanyan; Zhao, Tongzhi; Park, Myeongsam; Choi, Jaehwan; Li, Zhengqun
one_liner_zh: 该文用蛋白语言模型改造锰超氧化物歧化酶的热稳定性与活性，对象为酶蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，无结合建模或互作机制研究，与本课题无关。
abstract: Superoxide dismutases (SODs) are essential antioxidant enzymes that catalyze the dismutation of superoxide radicals, playing a crucial role in cellular defense against oxidative stress. However, most natural SODs lack the thermostability required for industrial and therapeutic applications. In this study, we identified a manganese-dependent SOD (PsSOD) from the extremophilic bacterium Pseudogracilibacillus sp., which exhibited high native activity but limited stability under high-temperature conditions. To enhance its robustness, we employed a protein language model-guided strategy that integrated PSSM, ESM-1v, and SaProt to predict thermostability-enhancing mutations. Through four rounds of rational design and combinatorial mutagenesis, we developed an optimized variant (M4: T19H/L90M/Q122K/A183I), which retained approximately 70 % of its activity after 1 h at 90  degrees C-a 1.8-fold improvement over the wild type. Moreover, its catalytic activity reached 1567.6 U/mg, representing a 2.2-fold enhancement compared to the wild-type enzyme. Structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that enhanced hydrophobic packing and reduced conformational flexibility contributed to the improved stability. Furthermore, M4 exhibited strong radical scavenging activity in vitro, activated the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta) in LPS-stimulated HaCaT and RAW264.7 cells. These results underscore the potential of AI-assisted protein engineering to develop robust antioxidant enzymes for biomedical, cosmetic, and industrial applications.
abstract_zh: 超氧化物歧化酶（SODs）是关键的抗氧化酶，催化超氧自由基的歧化反应，在细胞抵御氧化应激中发挥重要作用。然而，大多数天然SOD缺乏工业和治疗应用所需的热稳定性。在本研究中，我们从极端嗜热菌Pseudogracilibacillus sp.中鉴定出一种锰依赖性SOD（PsSOD），其具有较高的天然活性，但在高温条件下稳定性有限。为增强其稳健性，我们采用了一种蛋白质语言模型引导的策略，整合PSSM、ESM-1v和SaProt来预测提升热稳定性的突变。通过四轮理性设计和组合突变，我们开发了一个优化变体（M4: T19H/L90M/Q122K/A183I），其在90摄氏度下处理1小时后保留了约70%的活性，较野生型提高了1.8倍。此外，其催化活性达到1567.6 U/mg，较野生型酶增强了2.2倍。结构建模和分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟揭示，增强的疏水堆积和降低的构象柔性有助于提高稳定性。进一步地，M4在体外表现出强自由基清除活性，激活Nrf2/HO-1抗氧化通路，并在脂多糖刺激的HaCaT和RAW264.7细胞中抑制促炎细胞因子（IL-6、TNF-alpha、IL-1beta）。这些结果凸显了AI辅助蛋白质工程在开发用于生物医学、化妆品和工业应用的稳健抗氧化酶方面的潜力。
